subject: history
promptStrong: Give me an exam-style {board} {level} {subject} question on {lo}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a clear example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: In which region of England did the Pilgrimage of Grace mainly take place in 1536?
questions.explain: The Pilgrimage of Grace centred on the northern counties, especially Yorkshire, in late 1536.

questions.q: The Valor Ecclesiasticus of 1535 was a survey carried out for what purpose?
options: To plan a war with France
To assess the wealth of the Church before the dissolution
questions.explain: The Valor Ecclesiasticus valued Church property in 1535, preparing the way for the dissolution of the monasteries.

questions.q: What was Henry VIII's 'Great Matter'?
options: His attempt to annul his marriage to Catherine of Aragon
questions.explain: The 'Great Matter' was Henry's drawn-out effort to end his first marriage so he could marry Anne Boleyn.

questions.q: The Act of Supremacy, making Henry head of the Church in England, was passed in which year?
questions.explain: The Act of Supremacy of 1534 made Henry VIII Supreme Head of the Church of England.

questions.q: Which leader of the Pilgrimage of Grace was executed for treason in 1537?
questions.explain: Robert Aske, who led the Pilgrimage of Grace, was executed for treason in 1537 after the rising collapsed.

questions.q: What did the Act of Supremacy of 1534 declare Henry VIII to be?
options: Supreme Head of the Church of England
questions.explain: The 1534 Act declared Henry the Supreme Head of the Church of England, breaking from Rome.

questions.q: To whom had Catherine of Aragon first been married before Henry VIII?
questions.explain: Catherine had first married Henry's elder brother Arthur, whose death let Henry later marry her.

questions.q: What is the traditional rhyme summarising the fates of Henry VIII's six wives?
options: Married, exiled, married, exiled, crowned, died
Divorced, beheaded, died, divorced, beheaded, survived
Beheaded, divorced, survived, beheaded, died, married
Crowned, fought, prayed, fled, ruled, died
questions.explain: The rhyme runs 'divorced, beheaded, died, divorced, beheaded, survived'.

questions.q: Before becoming king, Henry VIII had originally been intended for what career?
questions.explain: As a younger son, Henry was reportedly destined for the Church until his elder brother Arthur died.

questions.q: Which Pope refused to grant Henry VIII the annulment of his first marriage?
questions.explain: Pope Clement VII refused to annul Henry's marriage to Catherine of Aragon, prompting the break with Rome.

questions.q: Anne Boleyn, Henry's second wife, met what fate in 1536?
questions.explain: Anne Boleyn was executed in 1536 on charges of adultery and treason.

questions.q: Who, as Archbishop of Canterbury, declared Henry's marriage to Catherine annulled in 1533?
questions.explain: Thomas Cranmer, made Archbishop in 1533, pronounced Henry's first marriage null and his marriage to Anne Boleyn valid.

questions.q: What policy, begun in 1536, saw monasteries closed and their wealth taken by the Crown?
questions.explain: The Dissolution of the Monasteries (from 1536) closed religious houses and transferred their wealth to Henry.

questions.q: Sir Thomas More was executed in 1535 for refusing to do what?
options: Accept Henry as Supreme Head of the Church
questions.explain: Thomas More was executed for refusing to swear the oath accepting Henry's supremacy over the Church.

questions.q: Why was a male heir so important to Henry VIII?
options: To secure the Tudor succession and avoid instability
questions.explain: Henry feared that without a son the Tudor dynasty might collapse into civil war, as in the Wars of the Roses.

questions.q: How many wives did Henry VIII have in total?
questions.explain: Henry VIII married six times: Catherine of Aragon, Anne Boleyn, Jane Seymour, Anne of Cleves, Catherine Howard and Catherine Parr.

questions.q: Which cardinal and Lord Chancellor fell from power after failing to secure Henry's divorce?
questions.explain: Cardinal Wolsey fell from power in 1529 after failing to obtain the annulment from the Pope.

questions.q: Who replaced Wolsey as Henry VIII's chief minister and organised the break with Rome?
questions.explain: Thomas Cromwell rose to become Henry's chief minister and engineered the break with Rome.

questions.q: Henry VIII's marriage to which wife led to Thomas Cromwell's downfall and execution in 1540?
questions.explain: The unpopular marriage to Anne of Cleves, which Cromwell arranged, helped bring about his fall and execution in 1540.

questions.q: Which wife gave Henry VIII his long-awaited male heir, the future Edward VI?
questions.explain: Jane Seymour gave birth to Edward VI in 1537 but died shortly afterwards.

questions.q: In which year did Henry VIII become King of England?
questions.explain: Henry VIII succeeded his father Henry VII in 1509.

questions.q: The Pilgrimage of Grace of 1536 was a rebellion against which policy?
options: Religious changes including the dissolution of monasteries
questions.explain: The Pilgrimage of Grace was a northern rising against Henry's religious reforms, especially the dissolution.
